narrative: Constructed 2026-08-29 as the worked example of the BROADSHEET language (the wider shelf). A fractional CFO and author who sells one thing: a written, argued plan. Speaks in numbered claims and short paragraphs; her clients are operators who read before they trust and arrive skeptical of anyone selling 'strategy'. Fills library holes: problem_first + practicing audience + serious_gravitas + editorial_columns density-as-respect with NO motion. Resulting direction: A PAGE YOU READ — paper ground, a masthead rule, three columns under a standfirst, one printer's red on exactly the words that matter; the argument IS the design. Teaches: the masthead-and-standfirst hero, column rhythm as hierarchy, a drop-cap as the only ornament, proof set as a table of figures, and the discipline of zero motion on a page that wants to be believed.

evidence: most owners can't tell you their gross margin by product line — that's the whole problem
they run a company already; they don't need a definition of cash flow
they've been sold strategy decks before
I tell them what the numbers say, not what they want them to say
it should feel like opening a financial paper, not a brochure
serif, restraint, figures — the conventions of trust in finance are kept
no logo yet, just my name
a 90-day plan, then the quarterly letters

palette.because: P4: a light room the skeptical reader sits inside; one printer's red spends only on the standfirst word and the single CTA (P3) — the eye learns red = the point.

typography.pairing_logic: One serif family at two sizes — kinship, not contrast — plus a small mono for figures and folios; expert_above (P5) is carried by scale and rules, not by a second face.
typography.because: A broadsheet is one voice at several sizes; a second display face would read as a brochure.

layout.because: P7: a practicing audience is paid in density — three text columns under a standfirst, hairlines between, a figures table on screen one.

motion.signature_move: none — the page holds still like print
motion.because: P8: motion has no thesis on a page that wants to be believed; stillness IS the claim.

hero_concept.concept_statement: A masthead rule, a dateline, then the problem stated as a headline in serif with a red standfirst beneath it; the first column starts immediately with a drop cap — the reader is already reading before they decide to.
hero_concept.because: problem_first + data_led → the statement is the image (P15: proof inside the first viewport as a small table of figures).

whitespace.because: Air lives between chapters (a hairline and a folio), never inside them — column measure ~62 characters, tight leading.

notes: numbered claims become numbered section folios (I, II, III) in the margin
every figure she cites is set in the mono at tabular width — numbers align like a ledger
the one testimonial runs as a pull-quote across two columns with the source set as a byline
'continued' links at column feet instead of buttons
voice_to_visual.because: A data-led voice becomes a typeset argument: measurements get tabular type, claims get folios.

rule_break.what: the hero has no image and no button above the fold — the first thing a visitor can do is read
rule_break.because: In a vertical of hero photos and 'Book a call', a page that opens with an argument is the one loud break (P10).

tension.expression: Gravitas owns the serif, the rules and the folios; directness owns the short paragraphs, the red standfirst and the figures table — one page, argued and typeset.
tension.because: Gravitas alone reads as a law firm; directness alone reads as a memo — she is both.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: Someone serious wrote this down and is prepared to be checked.
first_impression.remember: The red standfirst under the headline, and the little table of figures.
first_impression.because: serious_gravitas for a skeptical reader = evidence before persuasion.

language.because: A copy-rich advisor with one photo, a skeptical practicing audience and a data-led voice — the page should be read, not scrolled past; Ledger would be quieter than her claims, Signal too cool for paper trust.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Nearest is e2 (paper, serif, still, typographic) but differs on accent strategy (one red vs tonal), symmetry (three columns vs centred formal) and density (dense-as-respect vs balanced) — e2 is a calm room for the vulnerable, this is a paper for the skeptical.

banned_defaults_avoided: no centered hero over a photo

summary_for_practitioner: Your site reads like a good financial paper: a masthead rule, the problem stated plainly as the headline, a red standfirst under it, and then the argument in three columns with a small table of the figures you actually cite. One serif, one red, no animation — nothing moves because nothing needs to; the page is asking to be checked, not admired. Your numbered claims become numbered chapters in the margin, your one testimonial runs as a pull-quote with a byline, and the only button on the page comes after the reader has read.
